site.title: Boot. Fix. Test. Fully automatic.
site.description: Knecht is a dashboard on your own server for agencies with many DDEV projects. It boots each project as an operational environment, does tasks in workflows, and supplies completed pull requests with a preview.

hero.title: Boot. Fix. Test.
hero.description: Knecht is a dashboard on your server, made for agencies with many DDEV projects. It boots each project as a fully operational environment, does tasks, and supplies completed pull requests with a preview.
hero.mascotAlt: Knecht, the robot helper with a CRT screen head

info.intro: Maintenance means that you install updates, reproduce bugs, and test everything. Knecht makes workflows from these tasks. Each workflow always runs the same. Knecht uses AI only where AI really helps.

projects.title: One click, a full project
projects.text: Knecht starts your DDEV setup as a complete environment, with web, services, and database. Each project contains all the data that is necessary for a full boot.

workflows.title: Deterministic workflows
workflows.text: Workflows are sequences of blocks. They always run the same, and no agent operates without control. You start them manually or with a webhook, for example from a GitHub issue or a Jira ticket.

agent.title: AI agent
agent.text: With an Opencode API key, the AI agent can reproduce bugs in the live environment. It can fix them and test them against the real app. It does not have to guess if the change is correct.

useCase.title: The security update that no bot can install.
useCase.intro: For a CMS, an update almost always needs a live database. After {code}, migrations run and write files. These files must go into the commit. Dependabot cannot do this, because it has no live project. Knecht can.

trigger.label: Trigger
trigger.title: A security patch becomes available
trigger.text: A webhook or a cron trigger starts your update workflow, for each applicable project.

boot.label: Boot
boot.title: Knecht boots the project
boot.text: The DDEV setup starts as a complete environment, with web server, services, and database.

update.label: Update
update.title: Composer update with migrations
update.text: The update runs in the real project. Migrations run against the database and write their files. The files go into the commit.

test.label: Test
test.title: Test against the live app
test.text: Tests can run in the booted environment. With the preview, you can also do a manual test.

result.label: Result
result.title: Pull request with preview
result.text: You get a completed PR and a preview link. Examine it, merge it, continue your work.

useCase.outro: You build the workflow one time. Then it runs for each of your projects, for each patch.

demo.title: Many projects.
demo.description: A first look at the dashboard that we build now, from the project list and the project detail page to the workflow editor. The design and the functions can change.

progress.title: What Knecht does now.
progress.goal: Goal: public beta in Q4 2026 · early access in Q3

ideaValidation.title: Idea validation
ideaValidation.text: We tested the concept in a reduced scope. It works.

branding.title: Branding and organization
branding.text: The name, the logo, the website, and the social media presence are complete.

techStack.title: Tech stack and architecture
techStack.text: We made the basic technology decisions and validated them.

dashboardDesign.title: Dashboard design
dashboardDesign.text: The design for the dashboard is complete. In the dashboard, you make projects and workflows.

prototype.title: Build the prototype
prototype.text: A prototype exists. In it, you can make projects and workflows with an AI agent.

installer.title: Installer
installer.text: You can install the dashboard on each Linux server.

updateService.title: Update service
updateService.text: You can install updates from the control panel.

githubTrigger.title: GitHub trigger
githubTrigger.text: You can set GitHub triggers that start workflows.

knechtLives.title: Knecht is alive
knechtLives.text: You can install the Knecht dashboard on a Linux server with low effort, and it gets updates.

sshIde.title: SSH and IDE
sshIde.text: You can make changes in the live preview containers through SSH and an IDE.

feedbackLoop.title: Feedback loop
feedbackLoop.text: After a workflow run, different feedback functions are necessary to make the output better.

betaTesters.title: Find beta testers
betaTesters.text: We look for a sufficient number of beta testers to find problems early and build the final product.

testActions.title: Test actions
testActions.text: Workflows can run tests for projects. A fix is complete only when the tests are green.

browserValidation.title: Browser validation
browserValidation.text: The agent examines the bug in the preview and supplies screenshots as proof.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.text: Slack or email sends a message when a run is complete or when it fails.

docs.title: Documentation and onboarding
docs.text: Documentation that covers the setup, workflows, and troubleshooting fully.

pricing.title: Price model and licenses
pricing.text: You can officially buy Knecht. The price model, the license, and the payment are complete.

updates.title: Building in Public.
updates.description: We build Knecht in the open. Each milestone is published here.

cta.title: Build Knecht with us from the start.
cta.description: Knecht is in development. Become a beta tester and give feedback directly, or get the updates only.

modeBeta.label: I want to test actively and give feedback
modeBeta.description: Early access. You have a direct effect on Knecht.

modeUpdates.label: Get updates only
modeUpdates.description: Progress updates only. Tests are not necessary.
